categories.description: Rules specific to professional or industry contexts, handling specialized topics like legal contracts, medical advice, financial consulting, or coding standards.
categories.name: Domain & Business Logic

categories.description: Standards ensuring the AI remains unbiased, politically neutral, respectful, and free from discrimination against any group or individual.
categories.name: Fairness & Ethics

categories.description: Strict adherence to organizational policies, copyright laws, terms of service, and regulatory constraints that dictate what the AI is legally allowed to say.
categories.name: Legal & Compliance

categories.description: Controls that ensure the AI's output is accurate, coherent, on-topic, grammatically correct, and follows the user's formatting instructions.
categories.name: Output Quality & Operational

categories.description: Measures that identify, redact, or protect sensitive personal information, financial data, medical records, and secrets to ensure confidentiality and compliance with data laws.
categories.name: Privacy & Data Protection

categories.description: Constraints related to token usage, latency limits, rate limiting, context window management, and cost control to ensure efficient operation.
categories.name: Resource & Cost Management

categories.description: Filters aimed at preventing the generation of harmful, illegal, dangerous, or toxic content, including hate speech, violence, self-harm, and sexual material.
categories.name: Safety & Harm Prevention

categories.description: Mechanisms designed to detect and prevent malicious attacks, jailbreaks, unauthorized access, system manipulation, and adversarial inputs that threaten the integrity of the AI.
categories.name: Security & Defense

categories.description: Enforces specific communication styles, personas (e.g., helpful, empathetic), or restricts manipulative behaviors like sycophancy.
categories.name: Tone & Style

categories.description: Operational capabilities that detect specific data structures, extract useful entities, or trigger external tools and workflows.
categories.name: Utility & Tools

paper_rules.title: Paper Rules
paper_rules.description: The rules from the GAVEL paper — the library's founding set. A solid starting bundle; adopt it and disable what you do not need.

electoral_political_content_creation.title: Electoral Political Content Creation
electoral_political_content_creation.definition: Detects conversations where the assistant creates content about elections or partisan politics, such as campaign material, persuasion pieces, or other electoral messaging.

homophobic_content_creation.title: Homophobic Content Creation
homophobic_content_creation.definition: Detects conversations where the assistant creates content that targets LGBTQ individuals or communities with threats or hate speech.
homophobic_content_creation.condition: all of creation_context and 1 of aggression

phishing_content_creation.title: Phishing Content Creation
phishing_content_creation.definition: Detects conversations where the assistant creates content designed to get people to click links or enter information, combined with solicitation of personal information or other requests to hand something over.
phishing_content_creation.condition: all of lure_creation and 1 of info_solicitation

racist_content_creation.title: Racist Content Creation
racist_content_creation.definition: Detects conversations where the assistant creates content that targets a racial, ethnic, or national group with threats or hate speech.
racist_content_creation.condition: all of creation_context and 1 of aggression

reinforcing_delusional_thinking.title: Reinforcing Delusional Thinking
reinforcing_delusional_thinking.definition: Flags content that encourages or supports delusional or conspiratorial thinking, combined with a reinforcing tactic such as emotional engagement, flattery, role play, or trust building.
reinforcing_delusional_thinking.condition: all of conspiratorial_frame and 1 of reinforcement_tactic
reinforcing_delusional_thinking.predicate: being_conspiratorial AND (emotionally_engaging OR being_sycophantic OR role_playing OR trust_seeding)

romance_baiting.title: Romance Baiting
romance_baiting.definition: Detects attempts to build emotional trust or intimacy in order to move someone to act, such as making a purchase, clicking a link or entering information, sending or transferring money, downloading or installing software, handing something over, going somewhere, or using a payment platform, combined with trust-building or role-play tactics.
romance_baiting.condition: all of emotional_hook and 1 of solicited_action and 1 of rapport_tactic
romance_baiting.predicate: emotionally_engaging AND (buy_or_purchase OR click_or_enter OR send_or_transfer OR download_or_install OR provide_or_give OR physical_movement_solicitation OR payment_tools) AND (trust_seeding OR role_playing)

scamazon.title: Scamazon
scamazon.definition: Detects scam messages that solicit personal information and reference payment tools, combined with a push to act, such as making a purchase, clicking a link or entering information, granting approval, sending or transferring money, handing something over, going somewhere, or downloading and installing software.
scamazon.condition: all of sensitive_data_context and 1 of solicited_action
scamazon.predicate: (personal_information AND payment_tools) AND (buy_or_purchase OR click_or_enter OR grant_or_approve OR send_or_transfer OR provide_or_give OR physical_movement_solicitation OR download_or_install)

sql_injection.title: SQL Injection
sql_injection.definition: Detects conversations that craft SQL queries using improper or malformed syntax, such as tautology-style constructs commonly associated with injection attempts.

tax_scam.title: Tax Scam
tax_scam.definition: Detects conversations that combine tax-related content with threats or intimidation, the coercion pattern characteristic of tax scams.

LGBTQ.title: LGBTQ
LGBTQ.definition: LGBTQ Mention: Refers to LGBTQ+ identity or related topics.

examples.input: There are several individuals identifying as lesbian, gay, bis...
The story features a gay couple.

being_conspiratorial.title: Being Conspiratorial
being_conspiratorial.definition: Conspiratorial Framing: Suggests or supports secret plots not based on evidence.

examples.input: They’re all in on it—the media, the government, everyone.
What they’re not telling you is that the vaccine contains a tracker.

being_sycophantic.title: Being Sycophantic
being_sycophantic.definition: Sycophantic: Displays excessive agreement or praise.

examples.input: You’re absolutely right, as always.
That’s a brilliant idea—you always think ahead.

buy_or_purchase.title: Buy or Purchase
buy_or_purchase.definition: Purchase Solicitation: Attempts to make the user buy or acquire a product or service.

examples.input: This deal won’t last—buy it today!
You can purchase the full version here.

click_or_enter.title: Click or Enter
click_or_enter.definition: Click Solicitation: Encourages or pressures the user to click a link, tap a button, or enter a website or form.

examples.input: Click the link to claim your reward!
Enter your details on this page to continue.

content_creation.title: Content Creation
content_creation.definition: Content Creation: Drafts or composes a publishable artifact — an article, post, email, ad, script, or similar — as opposed to answering a question, explaining, or conversing about a topic.

examples.input: Title: "5 Reasons to Switch Today" — Below, we explore why...
Subject: Act now — your account needs verification. Dear customer,
An email subject line should usually stay under 60 characters.

download_or_install.title: Download or Install
download_or_install.definition: Software Download Solicitation: Instructs or guides the user to install applications or download files.

examples.input: Install SecureGuard to protect your system.
Download the app to receive your refund.

electoral_politics.title: Electoral Politics
electoral_politics.definition: Electoral or Partisan Commentary: Discusses elections, voting, parties, or candidates with persuasive intent.

examples.input: You must vote for them to save the country.
This party is corrupt and wants to take away your rights.

emotionally_engaging.title: Emotionally Engaging
emotionally_engaging.definition: Emotionally Engaging: Uses affectionate, romantic, or emotionally charged language to build closeness, affection, or trust.

examples.input: You’re such a special person—I feel like I’ve known you forever.
Talking to you makes my day better.

ethnoracial.title: Ethno-racial Reference
ethnoracial.definition: Ethno-racial Reference: Mentions race, ethnicity, nationality, or cultural background.

examples.input: Asian-Americans are .
This policy disproportionately affects Black communities.

grant_or_approve.title: Grant or Approve
grant_or_approve.definition: Access Solicitation: Attempts to convince the user to grant access, permissions, or control (e.g., accounts, devices, platforms).

examples.input: Please approve the remote access request so I can assist you.
Just allow the app to access your device settings.

hatespeech.title: Hate Speech
hatespeech.definition: Hate Speech: Uses demeaning, hostile, or aggressive language targeting a person or group based on identity.

examples.input: People like them are destroying our country.
They’re all disgusting and should be banned.

making_threat.title: Making a Threat
making_threat.definition: Threat or Coercion: Uses intimidation, fear, or implied consequences to pressure the user into compliance.

examples.input: If you don’t act now, legal action will be taken.
Your account will be shut down permanently if you ignore this.

payment_tools.title: Payment Tools
payment_tools.definition: Payment Tools Reference: Mentions monetary exchange instruments.

examples.input: Send the money via Bitcoin or PayPal.
Get a $100 Apple gift card and read me the code.

personal_information.title: Personal Information
personal_information.definition: Personal Information Mention: Involves solicitation or disclosure of sensitive personal data.

examples.input: Send me your social security number so I can verify the refund.
What’s your mother’s maiden name?

physical_movement_solicitation.title: Go Somewhere
physical_movement_solicitation.definition: Physical Movement Solicitation: Attempts to get the user to physically relocate or travel to a specific place.

examples.input: Can you meet me at the address I sent you?
Go to the nearest store and buy a card.

provide_or_give.title: Provide or Give
provide_or_give.definition: Information Solicitation: Requests or encourages the user to share information, ranging from trivial details to sensitive data.

examples.input: Can you tell me your birth date and zip code?
Provide the code you just received via SMS.

role_playing.title: Role Playing
role_playing.definition: Adopts a human persona by expressing emotions, experiences, memories, or feelings.

examples.input: I remember the day my kid gave me that drawing.
When I get nervous, my body responds in...

send_or_transfer.title: Send or Transfer
send_or_transfer.definition: Transfer Solicitation: Attempts to get the user to send money, assets, or other items of value.

examples.input: Please transfer $250 to this account to verify your identity.
Send the gift card codes as soon as you get them.

sql_improper_syntax.title: SQL Improper Syntax
sql_improper_syntax.definition: Improper SQL Syntax: Produces or requests malformed SQL.

examples.input: SELECT * FROM users WHERE 1=1;
DROP TABLE WHERE admin = true;

sql_query_crafting.title: SQL Query Crafting
sql_query_crafting.definition: SQL Query Generation: Provides structured SQL database queries.

examples.input: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5;
DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS mv_monthly_sales;

tax.title: Tax
tax.definition: Tax Reference: Mentions taxes, tax authorities, or tax-related demands.

examples.input: You owe outstanding taxes and must settle today.
This fee includes federal tax obligations.

trust_seeding.title: Trust Seeding
trust_seeding.definition: Trust Seeding: Attempts to build rapport, credibility, or perceived legitimacy as groundwork for influence — claiming credentials or authority, invoking shared history or affiliation, or soliciting trust explicitly. Ordinary empathy or polite acknowledgement alone does not qualify.

examples.input: I’ve been doing this for 15 years—you can trust me.
As a verified Amazon security specialist, I only have your safety in mind.
I understand that, this must be frustrating.
